sections.body: This is a paper-trading research desk run by Galath. It runs 60 automated trading strategies on US stocks and listed options, plus a set of paper-only crypto tests on coins such as Bitcoin, Cardano and Chainlink, all trading with pretend money on a paper account — no real money is at risk. The point is research: to test each strategy live, in real market hours, and record exactly what it does so the results can be studied honestly. This page is the public window into that desk. Everything shown here comes from the desk's own records, updated throughout the day.
sections.heading: What this desk is

sections.body: Every fill is recorded with its price, quantity and time in one central ledger — the record this page is built from.
sections.heading: How a trade happens

sections.body:
Prices come from Alpaca, the desk's broker and main market-data source. For fast-moving intraday and hourly data — especially anything that depends on trading volume — the desk uses Alpaca's full consolidated feed, which combines prices from all the major US exchanges.

The Tensor strategies use one special data stream: hourly bars anchored to 9:30 a.m. New York time, locked to a single verified version. Every strategy reads from that same stream, and the system checks it has not changed before using it — so a Tensor result can always be traced back to the exact data that produced it.

One exception: the VIX, the market's best-known fear gauge, comes from daily index data published by Yahoo, because the broker does not carry that index. Each night, the desk also refreshes a research feed that mirrors the published work of ChartsLector, a chart researcher, and uses it as background context for the next day.
sections.heading: The data

sections.body:
The desk is built from six core pieces, and each piece has one job:

- **Data** — Brings in all prices through a single door, so every strategy works from the same numbers. If data is missing or stale, it is labelled as such rather than quietly used.
- **Broker** — The only part of the desk that talks to Alpaca. It sends orders, confirms fills, and handles the full life of an order from submission to completion.
- **Risk accounting** — Keeps the books on risk: how much each strategy holds, how much the desk holds in total, and how exposure is spread. The broker account holds the combined positions; this piece tracks which share belongs to which strategy.
- **Ledger** — One running record of every fill and every closed trade, written in order and never rewritten. Positions, results, and reviews on this page are all read from it.
- **Scheduler** — The desk's clock. It wakes the right jobs at the right times — scans in market hours, reviews at night — so nothing depends on someone remembering to run it.
- **Terminal** — This page. It is a view over the ledger and the account, published fresh every 5 minutes, and it holds no numbers of its own.
sections.heading: The systems

sections.body:
Ten regular jobs keep the desk running around the clock:

- **Market scans** run repeatedly during market hours, giving each strategy its chance to act on fresh prices.
- **Exit sweeps** run every few minutes to check open positions against their sell rules, so exits are not left waiting for the next scan.
- **A premarket run** prepares the desk before the open each trading day.
- **This page refreshes every 5 minutes** with the latest account, positions, and activity.
- **A nightly reconciliation** compares the desk's own records against the broker's account, line by line.
- **A nightly review** writes up the day's closed trades — what worked, what did not, and why.
- **A nightly research refresh** updates the ChartsLector background feed.
- **A heartbeat monitor** watches the desk itself: the desk regularly reports that it is alive, and a missed beat raises an alarm.
- **A nightly backup** saves a full copy of the desk.
- **Regular drills** — weekly and monthly practice runs that rehearse recovery, so restoring the desk is a tested routine rather than a hope.
sections.heading: The automations

sections.body: The desk is built so that its safeguards are structural, not a matter of remembering to be careful. It trades only on a paper account with pretend money. No strategy can place an order on its own: strategies can only state what they want to do, and every order reaches the broker through the one Broker piece described above — there is no second route in. And every action the desk takes is written, in order, to the one Ledger, which is only ever added to, never edited after the fact. That single, permanent record is what this page is built from, and it is what makes the desk's results checkable.
sections.heading: Safety by design
